title: identity-context-svc (GOV-01)
description: GOV-01 Tenant Context & Resolution. The service-golden-signals dashboard covers RED metrics for every service; this one covers what is specific to GOV-01 and cannot be inferred from request rates — the outbox depth, the security refusals, and the break-glass grants.

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Tier 0. Nothing on the platform authenticates while this is down.

panels.title: Resolve latency (P50 / P95 / P99)
panels.description: The 50ms P99 target from the resolver's own doc comment. The in-process portion is guarded in CI by internal/context/nfr_test.go; this is the end-to-end number, which includes the two registry round trips and the Postgres evidence write that the unit test stubs out.

panels.title: Resolution outcomes
panels.description: A rising 401 rate with a flat 200 rate is credential stuffing. A rising 503 rate is an upstream, not a client.

panels.title: Outbox — the signal that is invisible from the request path
Outbox pending depth
panels.description: THE number to alert on. Everything else about this service can look perfectly healthy while governance events pile up in a table, because a stopped relay is invisible from the request path. A short spike during a broker restart is the outbox doing its job; a line that only goes up is the relay not running.

panels.title: Outbox dead letters
panels.description: Events that exhausted their retries. They are NOT deleted — they stay in event_outbox with last_error set, which is how you find them. Any non-zero value needs a human; a restart will not fix one. See docs/runbook.md, 'Outbox dead letters'.

panels.title: Ingress / tenant mismatches
panels.description: A request arriving on tenant A's hostname bearing tenant B's token. There is no legitimate request of this shape: it is either a routing misconfiguration serving one customer's hostname to another's backend, or somebody probing the boundary. Any sustained non-zero rate is a page, not a ticket.

panels.title: Residency denials
panels.description: An entity whose data residency policy this region may not serve. Expect zero. A non-zero rate after a deploy usually means ALLOWED_RESIDENCY_POLICIES was not updated for the region, not that anybody did anything wrong.

panels.title: Risk signal availability
panels.description: A sustained 'unavailable' rate means the Intelligence Plane is not publishing session.risk.changed, so every session's posture is DEFAULTED to STANDARD rather than measured. This used to be self-silencing — the service published the alarm on the same topic it consumed risk signals from, and answered its own alarm.

panels.title: Live support contexts
panels.description: Privileged elevations into customer tenants that are active right now. In steady state this is zero. Every one is scoped, time-limited, independently approved and evidenced — but it is still somebody with standing inside a customer's data.

panels.title: Awaiting review
panels.description: Support contexts that have ENDED and were never reconciled. This is the half of break-glass that is normally missing: the grant expires, nobody looks, and the control is decorative. Non-zero for more than a working day is a process failure, not a system one.

panels.title: Segregation-of-duties outcomes
panels.description: Conflicts are the control working. UNAVAILABLE is the control NOT working: the command was refused, which is correct, but a sustained rate means GOV-04 is down and privileged commands cannot be issued at all.

panels.title: Disposition: disposed vs held back
panels.description: These two must be read together. A sweep that disposed nothing because everything was held by a legal hold looks identical to a quiet night if you only watch the disposed count.
